Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah, who said: ﴿nor would He have made it known to you﴾ means: nor would He have made you aware of it.

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Abbas that he used to read: ﴿nor would I have warned you thereby﴾ (wa-la anzartukum bihi).

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿Indeed I have lived among you a lifetime before it﴾ that he said: "I did not recite it to you, nor did I mention it."

Both of them also narrated from him that he said: He lived forty years before he was inspired. He saw the true dream for two years, and Allah inspired him for ten years in Makkah and ten years in Madinah. He died at the age of sixty-two.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, was sent at forty. He remained in Makkah for thirteen years during which revelation came to him. Then he was commanded to emigrate, and he emigrated for ten years, and he died at the age of sixty-three.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 10, verses 11–16 (part 1 of 2):

When Allah, glorified is He, mentioned the threat concerning disbelief in the Return (al-ma'ad), He mentioned that this punishment is due to be delayed beyond this worldly life.

Al-Qaffal said: When He described them as heedless, He reinforced this by stating that the extent of their heedlessness is that whenever the Messenger warned them, they demanded the punishment hastily. Allah, glorified is He, then made clear that there is no benefit in bringing evil upon them, so that perhaps they would repent and from their loins there would come forth one who believes.

It has been said: the meaning of ﴿And if Allah were to hasten for people the evil as they seek to hasten the good﴾ is: if Allah were to hasten punishment for people as they hasten for reward and good. ﴿Their term would have been decreed for them﴾ means they would have died. It has also been said: the meaning is that if Allah dealt with people in responding to them with what is disliked as He would deal with them in responding to them with what is good, He would have destroyed them. It has also been said: the verse is specific to the disbelievers who denied the resurrection and what follows from it.

In al-Kashshaf it says: "The hastening for good was placed in the position of Allah hastening good for them, to indicate the swiftness of His response and His granting of their request, so that their hastening for good is as if it were His hastening of it."  The intended people are the people of Makkah, and His saying: ﴿So rain down upon us stones from the sky﴾ [al-Anfal: 32], and so on.

It has been said: the implied meaning is: "And if Allah were to hasten for them the evil when they seek it with a hastening like His hastening of good for them when they seek it," so what was omitted was omitted because the remaining part indicates it.

Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: There is an omission in the speech. The implied meaning is ﴿And if Allah were to hasten for people the evil﴾ with a hastening like ﴿their seeking of good﴾. Then he omitted "hastening" (ta'jil) and placed its attribute in its position, then he omitted the attribute and placed the genitive noun that is attached to it in its position. He said: This is the view of al-Khalil and Sibawayh, and it is the saying of al-Akhfash and al-Farra'. They said: its original form is "like their seeking," then the kaf was removed and the noun was put in the accusative.

Al-Farra' said: Just as you say, "I struck Zayd a striking of yours," meaning "like your striking." The meaning of ﴿their term would have been decreed for them﴾ is "they would have been destroyed," but He, glorified is He, did not hasten evil for them, so they were given respite. It has also been said its meaning is: they would have been made to die.

Ibn 'Amir read "laqada" (لَقَضى) in the active voice, and this is a good reading because it suits His saying: ﴿if Allah were to hasten﴾.

His saying: ﴿So We leave those who do not expect a meeting with Us in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ — the fa' is for coordination with an implied element indicated by the speech, because His saying ﴿if Allah were to hasten﴾ implies the negation of hastening, so it is as if it were said: "But He does not hasten evil for them nor decree their term, so We leave them," etc.: that is, We leave them and give them respite. Al-tughyan means exaggeration, which is elevation and rising. The meaning of ya'mahun (يَعْمَهُونَ) is "they wander in confusion": that is, We leave them wandering in confusion in their arrogance, their haughtiness, and their refusal to accept the truth, as a means of luring them and as abandonment.

Then Allah, glorified is He, made clear that they are liars in seeking evil. Had what they asked for befallen them, they would have shown helplessness and distress. So He said: ﴿And when harm touches man﴾, that is, this kind [of human being], which is true of every situation in which harm occurs, ﴿he calls upon Us for his side﴾. The lam is for time, like His saying "I came to him for the month of such-and-such." Or it is in the position of an accusative as a circumstantial clause, as indicated by the coordination of ("sitting or standing") with it, and the lam would then mean "upon": that is, he calls upon Us lying on his side, ﴿or sitting or standing﴾. It is as if He said: he calls upon Us in all the aforementioned states and others, and He singled out the mentioned ones because they are the most common states for a human being, while others are rare, such as bowing and prostration. It is also permissible that it means he calls upon Allah while lying down unable to sit, sitting unable to stand, and standing unable to walk, but the first is better.

Al-Zajjaj said: Enumerating the states of supplication is more eloquent than enumerating the states of harm, because if he is supplicating constantly, and then forgets in the time of ease, that is more astonishing.

His saying: ﴿Then when We remove from him his harm, he passes on as if he had never called Us to a harm that touched him﴾ — that is: when We remove from him the harm that touched him, as the fa' indicates, he goes on in his way which he had been upon before harm touched him, and he forgets the state of hardship and trial; or he passes on from the position of supplication and humility and does not return to it, as if he had no covenant with it, as if he had not called upon Us when harm touched him for the removal of that harm which had touched him.

It has been said: the meaning of "marra" (passed on) is that he persisted in his disbelief and did not give thanks and did not take heed.

Al-Akhfash said: The "an" in ﴿as if he had not called﴾ is the lightened form of the heavy one, and the meaning is: "as if he." End of quote.

The comparative clause is in the position of an accusative as a circumstantial clause.

This state which Allah mentioned for the supplicant is not restricted to the people of disbelief; rather it occurs among many Muslims too, whose tongues grow soft with supplication and whose hearts with humility and submission when what they dislike descends upon them. Then when Allah removes it from them, they become heedless of supplication and humility, and they forget what is obligatory upon them of thanking for the blessing that Allah bestowed upon them by answering their supplication, lifting the harm that had descended upon them, and repelling the disliked matter that had befallen them.

This is among what indicates that the verse covers both the Muslim and the disbeliever, as the wording "for people" (lin-nas) and the word "man" (al-insan) suggests. O Allah, inspire us to thank You for Your blessings, and remind us of the states in which You favored us by answering supplication, until we multiply thanks that we cannot bear to be without, and cannot manage otherwise. How free You are of it and how much we need it! And ﴿If you are grateful, I will surely increase you﴾ [Ibrahim: 7].

The indication in His saying: ﴿Thus was made attractive to the transgressors what they were doing﴾ refers to the verbal noun of the verb mentioned after it, as has passed more than once: that is, like that wondrous adornment, their deeds were made attractive to the transgressors.

The musrif in the language is one who spends much wealth for a base purpose. The position of "thus" (kadhalika) is accusative as an adverb of manner (masdariyya).

The adornment is either from Allah, Exalted, by way of embellishment and withholding gentleness from them, or by way of Satan through whisperings, or by way of the commanding self (al-nafs al-ammara bi'l-su').

The meaning is that He made attractive to them turning away from supplication, heedlessness of gratitude, and preoccupation with desires.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned what serves as a deterrent and reproach against what these people had done, and said: ﴿And We had destroyed the generations before you when they wronged﴾ — meaning the past nations before these disbelievers contemporary with the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family: that is, We destroyed them before your time. It has been said: the address is to the people of Makkah by way of iltifat for the sake of emphasis in rebuke. "Lamma" is a temporal adverb for "We destroyed," meaning: We destroyed them when they committed wrong by denying, by mocking the Messengers, and by excess in sins, without delaying their destruction, as We have delayed your destruction. The waw in ﴿and their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾ is circumstantial, with "qad" implied: that is, and their messengers whom We had sent to them had come to them with clear proofs, that is, with clear verses evident in indicating the truthfulness of the Messengers. It has been said: the waw is for coordination with "they wronged," and the first is better. It has also been said: the wrong here means polytheism, and the waw in ﴿and they would not have believed﴾ is for coordination with "they wronged," or the clause is parenthetical, and the lam is for emphasis of negation: that is, it was not valid nor proper for them to believe, due to their lack of readiness for that and the withholding of divine favours from them. ﴿Thus do We recompense the criminal people﴾: that is, like that recompense We recompense the criminal people, which is total uprooting for every criminal. This is a severe threat for whoever was among the disbelievers of his time, or for the disbelievers of Makkah specifically.

Then Allah, glorified is He, addressed those to whom the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, was sent, saying: ﴿Then We made you successors (khala'if)﴾ — that is, We made you successors on the earth after those generations whose reports you hear and whose traces you see. Khala'if is the plural of khalifa, and the discussion of it has already passed at the end of Surat al-An'am. The lam in ﴿that We might observe how you would do﴾ is the lam of purpose: that is, in order that We might observe how you would act, of good and evil deeds. "Kayfa" is in the accusative position governed by the verb after it: that is, that We might observe what deed you do; or it is in the accusative position as a circumstantial state: that is, in what condition you do the deeds fitting for succession.

Then Allah, glorified is He, related a third type of their obstinacy and their trifling with the signs of Allah, and said: ﴿And when Our verses are recited to them as clear evidences﴾ — there is a shift from address to the third person, in turning away from them. The intended verses are the verses in the Noble Book: that is, when the reciter recites upon them Our verses indicating the affirmation of monotheism and the nullification of polytheism, being clear in indicating what is sought. ﴿Those who do not expect a meeting with Us say﴾ — and they are the deniers of the Return, whose interpretation has passed shortly before: that is, they said to the one who recites them to them, who is the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family: ﴿Bring a Qur'an other than this, or change it.﴾ When they heard what enraged them in what he recited to them of the Qur'an, of reproach of idol-worship and severe warning to whoever worships them, they requested of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, one of two things: either to bring a Qur'an other than this Qur'an while this Qur'an remains as it is, or to replace this Qur'an by abrogating some or all of its verses and putting others in their place that agree with their desire and suit their purpose. So Allah commanded him to say in reply to them: ﴿It is not for me﴾ — that is, it is not fitting for me nor lawful for me that I change it of my own accord. Thus he negated from himself one of the two options, which is the substitution, because it is the one that would be possible for him were that permissible, unlike the other option, which is bringing another Qur'an, for that is not within his capacity and he cannot do it.

It has been said: he, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, negated from himself the easier of the two options so that it would serve as evidence for negating the harder of them by a fortiori reasoning. This was from him, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, by way of humouring the foolish, since such a suggestion would not come from sensible people after Allah had commanded him in this matter, and He, glorified is He, knows best the interests of His servants and what would repel the disbelievers from these worthless requests and cold questions. "Tilqa'" is a verbal noun used as an adverb, meaning "from my own side."

Al-Zajjaj said: They asked him to drop what it contains of mention of the Resurrection and the Rising. It has been said: they asked him to drop what it contains of the faults of their deities and the foolishness of their intellects. It has been said: they asked him to turn the promise into a threat, and the forbidden into the lawful and the lawful into the forbidden. Then He commanded him to affirm what he answered them with, namely that it was neither valid nor proper for him to replace it of his own accord, by His saying: ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me﴾: that is, I follow nothing of things except what is revealed to me from Allah, glorified is He, without substitution, alteration, distortion, or corruption. Thus He confined his state, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, to following what is revealed to him. Perhaps the disbelievers' intent in this question was to insinuate to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, that the Qur'an was his own speech, and that he was able to bring another or to change it.

Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded him to say to them, completing the answer to them: ﴿Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous day.﴾ For this sentence serves as a justification for what he had presented as an answer before it. The tremendous day is the Day of Resurrection: that is, ﴿Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord﴾ by doing what you demand, on the assumption that it is possible, ﴿the punishment of the Day of Resurrection.﴾

Then He, glory be to Him, affirmed that this Qur'an is from Allah, and that he, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, conveys to them only what Allah commanded him to convey, and he is not able to do otherwise. So He said: ﴿Say: "If Allah had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you through me."﴾ That is, this Qur'an recited to you is by the will and volition of Allah. Had Allah willed that I not recite it to you and not convey it to you, I would not have recited it. The whole matter is subject to the will of Allah; I have no part in it. His words ﴿nor would He have made it known to you through me﴾ are coordinated with what precedes, "I would not have recited it." That is, had Allah willed, He would not have made you aware of the Qur'an through me. It is said: "I knew (dart) the thing, and Allah made me know it (adrani-hu Allah)."

The majority of readers recited it with an alif in أدراكم, from أدراه يُدريه, meaning "he informed him, he makes him know."

Ibn Kathir recited ﴿wa-la-adra-kum bihi﴾ without an alif between the lam and the hamza. The meaning is: had Allah willed, He would have made you know of it without my reciting it to you. The lam here is the emphatic lam (lam al-ta'kid), which entered on the alif of af'ala (the verb form).

It has also been read as أَدْرَؤُكم with a hamza. It was said that this hamza is changed from an alif, since both come from the same root. It may also be from دَرَأْتُهُ, meaning "I repelled him," and أَدْرَأْتُهُ, meaning "I made him a disputant (dari)." The meaning is: I would make you adversaries who would repel me with argument and call me a liar, by means of its recitation.

Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan read ﴿wa-la-adra-tukum bihi﴾. Abu Hatim said: its origin is ولا أدريتكم به, and the ya' was replaced by an alif. Al-Nahhas said: this is an error. The transmission from al-Hasan is ولا أدرأتكم with a hamza.

His words ﴿Indeed I have lived among you a lifetime before it﴾ are a reason for the claim that this is by the will of Allah, and the Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, had no role except conveying. That is: I have remained among you for a long period before it, that is, a long time. It was forty years before the Qur'an. You know me for truthfulness and trustworthiness. I am not one who reads, nor one who writes. ﴿Will you not then use your reason?﴾ The hamza here is for rebuke and reproach. That is: will you not act in accordance with what reason requires, namely not denying me in the face of what you have known of my continuous habit over a long period, of truthfulness and trustworthiness, and of my not reading the books revealed to the messengers, and not learning what their people know of knowledge, nor seeking or desiring anything of this matter? Then I came to you with this Book, which you were unable to match with a single surah, and you fell short of contending with it, though you are the Arabs, witnessed to have perfect eloquence, and acknowledged to have reached in it a level that no one else reaches?

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿If Allah were to hasten for people the evil...﴾ up to the end of the verse, that he said: it is a person's saying to his child or his property when he is angry with them: "O Allah, do not bless him, and curse him." ﴿Their term would have been decreed for them﴾: he said: [Allah would have] destroyed the one against whom he invoked, and caused him to die.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding the verse, that he said: it is a man's saying to another man, "O Allah, curse him, O Allah, disgrace him," while he loves that it be answered for him.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatadah, regarding the verse, that he said: it is a man's supplication against himself and his property with what he dislikes, that it be answered for him.

Al-Qurtubi related in his tafsir (exegesis) from Ibn Ishaq and Muqatil regarding the verse that both said: it is the saying of al-Nadr ibn al-Harith: ﴿O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky﴾ [al-Anfal: 32]. Had Allah hastened this for them, they would have been destroyed.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Juraij regarding His words ﴿who calls Us when he is lying on his side﴾ that he said: lying down.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿who calls Us when he is lying on his side, or sitting, or standing﴾ that he said: in every state.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Abu al-Darda', who said: Call upon Allah in your days of ease, and He will answer you in your days of hardship.

I say: Increase your thanks to Allah for ease, and He will repel hardship from you. For His promise to the grateful of increased blessings indicates that He will repel calamities from them, because the sweetness of blessing is lost when the bitterness of calamity is present. O Allah, gather for us between attracting blessings and removing calamities, for we thank You as many times as the grateful have thanked You, with every tongue, in every age, and we praise You as many times as the praisers have praised You, with every tongue, in every age. (p-616)

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿Then We made you successors in the earth﴾ up to the end of the verse, that he said: It has been related to us that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) recited this verse and said: "Our Lord has spoken the truth. He made us successors in the earth only so that He might see our deeds. So show Allah the best of your deeds, by night and by day, in secret and in public."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Juraij, who said: ﴿successors in the earth﴾ refers to the community (ummah) of Muhammad, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿Bring a Qur'an other than this, or change it﴾ that he said: this is the saying of the polytheists of Makkah to the Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿nor would He have made it known to you through me﴾ that it means: "made you know of it."

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah, who said: ﴿nor would He have made it known to you﴾ means: nor would He have made you aware of it.

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Abbas that he used to read: ﴿nor would I have warned you thereby﴾ (wa-la anzartukum bihi).

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿Indeed I have lived among you a lifetime before it﴾ that he said: "I did not recite it to you, nor did I mention it."

Both of them also narrated from him that he said: He lived forty years before he was inspired. He saw the true dream for two years, and Allah inspired him for ten years in Makkah and ten years in Madinah. He died at the age of sixty-two.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, was sent at forty. He remained in Makkah for thirteen years during which revelation came to him. Then he was commanded to emigrate, and he emigrated for ten years, and he died at the age of sixty-three.

O Allah, inspire us to thank You for Your blessings, and remind us of the states in which You favored us by answering supplication, until we multiply thanks that we cannot bear to be without, and cannot manage otherwise. How free You are of it and how much we need it! And ﴿If you are grateful, I will surely increase you﴾ [Ibrahim: 7].

The indication in His saying: ﴿Thus was made attractive to the transgressors what they were doing﴾ refers to the verbal noun of the verb mentioned after it, as has passed more than once: that is, like that wondrous adornment, their deeds were made attractive to the transgressors.

The musrif in the language is one who spends much wealth for a base purpose. The position of "thus" (kadhalika) is accusative as an adverb of manner (masdariyya).

The adornment is either from Allah, Exalted, by way of embellishment and withholding gentleness from them, or by way of Satan through whisperings, or by way of the commanding self (al-nafs al-ammara bi'l-su').

The meaning is that He made attractive to them turning away from supplication, heedlessness of gratitude, and preoccupation with desires.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned what serves as a deterrent and reproach against what these people had done, and said: ﴿And We had destroyed the generations before you when they wronged﴾ — meaning the past nations before these disbelievers contemporary with the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family: that is, We destroyed them before your time. It has been said: the address is to the people of Makkah by way of iltifat for the sake of emphasis in rebuke. "Lamma" is a temporal adverb for "We destroyed," meaning: We destroyed them when they committed wrong by denying, by mocking the Messengers, and by excess in sins, without delaying their destruction, as We have delayed your destruction. The waw in ﴿and their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾ is circumstantial, with "qad" implied: that is, and their messengers whom We had sent to them had come to them with clear proofs, that is, with clear verses evident in indicating the truthfulness of the Messengers. It has been said: the waw is for coordination with "they wronged," and the first is better. It has also been said: the wrong here means polytheism, and the waw in ﴿and they would not have believed﴾ is for coordination with "they wronged," or the clause is parenthetical, and the lam is for emphasis of negation: that is, it was not valid nor proper for them to believe, due to their lack of readiness for that and the withholding of divine favours from them. ﴿Thus do We recompense the criminal people﴾: that is, like that recompense We recompense the criminal people, which is total uprooting for every criminal. This is a severe threat for whoever was among the disbelievers of his time, or for the disbelievers of Makkah specifically.

Then Allah, glorified is He, addressed those to whom the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, was sent, saying: ﴿Then We made you successors (khala'if)﴾ — that is, We made you successors on the earth after those generations whose reports you hear and whose traces you see. Khala'if is the plural of khalifa, and the discussion of it has already passed at the end of Surat al-An'am. The lam in ﴿that We might observe how you would do﴾ is the lam of purpose: that is, in order that We might observe how you would act, of good and evil deeds. "Kayfa" is in the accusative position governed by the verb after it: that is, that We might observe what deed you do; or it is in the accusative position as a circumstantial state: that is, in what condition you do the deeds fitting for succession.

Then Allah, glorified is He, related a third type of their obstinacy and their trifling with the signs of Allah, and said: ﴿And when Our verses are recited to them as clear evidences﴾ — there is a shift from address to the third person, in turning away from them. The intended verses are the verses in the Noble Book: that is, when the reciter recites upon them Our verses indicating the affirmation of monotheism and the nullification of polytheism, being clear in indicating what is sought. ﴿Those who do not expect a meeting with Us say﴾ — and they are the deniers of the Return, whose interpretation has passed shortly before: that is, they said to the one who recites them to them, who is the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family: ﴿Bring a Qur'an other than this, or change it.﴾ When they heard what enraged them in what he recited to them of the Qur'an, of reproach of idol-worship and severe warning to whoever worships them, they requested of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, one of two things: either to bring a Qur'an other than this Qur'an while this Qur'an remains as it is, or to replace this Qur'an by abrogating some or all of its verses and putting others in their place that agree with their desire and suit their purpose. So Allah commanded him to say in reply to them: ﴿It is not for me﴾ — that is, it is not fitting for me nor lawful for me that I change it of my own accord. Thus he negated from himself one of the two options, which is the substitution, because it is the one that would be possible for him were that permissible, unlike the other option, which is bringing another Qur'an, for that is not within his capacity and he cannot do it.

It has been said: he, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, negated from himself the easier of the two options so that it would serve as evidence for negating the harder of them by a fortiori reasoning. This was from him, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, by way of humouring the foolish, since such a suggestion would not come from sensible people after Allah had commanded him in this matter, and He, glorified is He, knows best the interests of His servants and what would repel the disbelievers from these worthless requests and cold questions. "Tilqa'" is a verbal noun used as an adverb, meaning "from my own side."

Al-Zajjaj said: They asked him to drop what it contains of mention of the Resurrection and the Rising. It has been said: they asked him to drop what it contains of the faults of their deities and the foolishness of their intellects. It has been said: they asked him to turn the promise into a threat, and the forbidden into the lawful and the lawful into the forbidden. Then He commanded him to affirm what he answered them with, namely that it was neither valid nor proper for him to replace it of his own accord, by His saying: ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me﴾: that is, I follow nothing of things except what is revealed to me from Allah, glorified is He, without substitution, alteration, distortion, or corruption. Thus He confined his state, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, to following what is revealed to him. Perhaps the disbelievers' intent in this question was to insinuate to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, that the Qur'an was his own speech, and that he was able to bring another or to change it.

Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded him to say to them, completing the answer to them: ﴿Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous day.﴾ For this sentence serves as a justification for what he had presented as an answer before it. The tremendous day is the Day of Resurrection: that is, ﴿Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord﴾ by doing what you demand, on the assumption that it is possible, ﴿the punishment of the Day of Resurrection.﴾

Then He, glory be to Him, affirmed that this Qur'an is from Allah, and that he, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, conveys to them only what Allah commanded him to convey, and he is not able to do otherwise. So He said: ﴿Say: "If Allah had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you through me."﴾ That is, this Qur'an recited to you is by the will and volition of Allah. Had Allah willed that I not recite it to you and not convey it to you, I would not have recited it. The whole matter is subject to the will of Allah; I have no part in it. His words ﴿nor would He have made it known to you through me﴾ are coordinated with what precedes, "I would not have recited it." That is, had Allah willed, He would not have made you aware of the Qur'an through me. It is said: "I knew (dart) the thing, and Allah made me know it (adrani-hu Allah)."

The majority of readers recited it with an alif in أدراكم, from أدراه يُدريه, meaning "he informed him, he makes him know."

Ibn Kathir recited ﴿wa-la-adra-kum bihi﴾ without an alif between the lam and the hamza. The meaning is: had Allah willed, He would have made you know of it without my reciting it to you. The lam here is the emphatic lam (lam al-ta'kid), which entered on the alif of af'ala (the verb form).

It has also been read as أَدْرَؤُكم with a hamza. It was said that this hamza is changed from an alif, since both come from the same root. It may also be from دَرَأْتُهُ, meaning "I repelled him," and أَدْرَأْتُهُ, meaning "I made him a disputant (dari)." The meaning is: I would make you adversaries who would repel me with argument and call me a liar, by means of its recitation.

Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan read ﴿wa-la-adra-tukum bihi﴾. Abu Hatim said: its origin is ولا أدريتكم به, and the ya' was replaced by an alif. Al-Nahhas said: this is an error. The transmission from al-Hasan is ولا أدرأتكم with a hamza.

His words ﴿Indeed I have lived among you a lifetime before it﴾ are a reason for the claim that this is by the will of Allah, and the Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, had no role except conveying. That is: I have remained among you for a long period before it, that is, a long time. It was forty years before the Qur'an. You know me for truthfulness and trustworthiness. I am not one who reads, nor one who writes. ﴿Will you not then use your reason?﴾ The hamza here is for rebuke and reproach. That is: will you not act in accordance with what reason requires, namely not denying me in the face of what you have known of my continuous habit over a long period, of truthfulness and trustworthiness, and of my not reading the books revealed to the messengers, and not learning what their people know of knowledge, nor seeking or desiring anything of this matter? Then I came to you with this Book, which you were unable to match with a single surah, and you fell short of contending with it, though you are the Arabs, witnessed to have perfect eloquence, and acknowledged to have reached in it a level that no one else reaches?

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿If Allah were to hasten for people the evil...﴾ up to the end of the verse, that he said: it is a person's saying to his child or his property when he is angry with them: "O Allah, do not bless him, and curse him." ﴿Their term would have been decreed for them﴾: he said: [Allah would have] destroyed the one against whom he invoked, and caused him to die.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding the verse, that he said: it is a man's saying to another man, "O Allah, curse him, O Allah, disgrace him," while he loves that it be answered for him.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatadah, regarding the verse, that he said: it is a man's supplication against himself and his property with what he dislikes, that it be answered for him.

Al-Qurtubi related in his tafsir (exegesis) from Ibn Ishaq and Muqatil regarding the verse that both said: it is the saying of al-Nadr ibn al-Harith: ﴿O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky﴾ [al-Anfal: 32]. Had Allah hastened this for them, they would have been destroyed.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Juraij regarding His words ﴿who calls Us when he is lying on his side﴾ that he said: lying down.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿who calls Us when he is lying on his side, or sitting, or standing﴾ that he said: in every state.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Abu al-Darda', who said: Call upon Allah in your days of ease, and He will answer you in your days of hardship.

I say: Increase your thanks to Allah for ease, and He will repel hardship from you. For His promise to the grateful of increased blessings indicates that He will repel calamities from them, because the sweetness of blessing is lost when the bitterness of calamity is present. O Allah, gather for us between attracting blessings and removing calamities, for we thank You as many times as the grateful have thanked You, with every tongue, in every age, and we praise You as many times as the praisers have praised You, with every tongue, in every age. (p-616)

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿Then We made you successors in the earth﴾ up to the end of the verse, that he said: It has been related to us that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) recited this verse and said: "Our Lord has spoken the truth. He made us successors in the earth only so that He might see our deeds. So show Allah the best of your deeds, by night and by day, in secret and in public."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Juraij, who said: ﴿successors in the earth﴾ refers to the community (ummah) of Muhammad, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿Bring a Qur'an other than this, or change it﴾ that he said: this is the saying of the polytheists of Makkah to the Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿nor would He have made it known to you through me﴾ that it means: "made you know of it."

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah, who said: ﴿nor would He have made it known to you﴾ means: nor would He have made you aware of it.

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Abbas that he used to read: ﴿nor would I have warned you thereby﴾ (wa-la anzartukum bihi).

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿Indeed I have lived among you a lifetime before it﴾ that he said: "I did not recite it to you, nor did I mention it."

Both of them also narrated from him that he said: He lived forty years before he was inspired. He saw the true dream for two years, and Allah inspired him for ten years in Makkah and ten years in Madinah. He died at the age of sixty-two.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, was sent at forty. He remained in Makkah for thirteen years during which revelation came to him. Then he was commanded to emigrate, and he emigrated for ten years, and he died at the age of sixty-three.

The Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on Surah 10, verses 17–19:

His saying: ﴿Who does greater wrong than one who invents a lie against Allah?﴾ This is an interrogative with the sense of negation, meaning: no one does greater wrong than one who ﴿invents a lie against Allah﴾. The addition of *kadhiban* (a lie) although *iftira'* (invention) is never anything but a lie serves to show that this, besides being an invention against Allah, is a lie in itself. For an invention may be a lie only in its attribution, as when the sin of Zayd is attributed to 'Amr. Abu al-Su'ud mentioned the meaning of this in his tafsir. It has been said: this is part of his (ﷺ) response to the polytheists when they asked him to bring a Qur'an other than this Qur'an, or to change it. So He made clear to them that if he did that, it would be an invention against Allah, and no wrong is comparable to it. It has also been said: those who invent a lie against Allah are the polytheists, and those who deny the signs of Allah are the People of the Book. ﴿Indeed, the criminals will not succeed.﴾ This is a justification for the statement that there is no one more wrong than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies His signs. That is: they will not attain their objective, nor will they gain any good. The pronoun in *innahu* (indeed it) refers to the matter (*li-l-sha'n*), meaning: indeed the matter is this.

Then Allah, glorified is He, censured them for worshipping idols, and made clear that they neither benefit those who worship them nor harm those who do not worship them. So He said: ﴿And they worship besides Allah﴾, that is, transgressing beyond Allah, glorified is He, to worship others, not in the sense of abandoning His worship altogether. ﴿That which neither harms them nor benefits them﴾, that is, that which by its nature has neither harm nor benefit. It is the right of the one worshipped to reward those who obey him and punish those who disobey him. The *wa* (and) is for conjoining this sentence to the sentence ﴿And when Our signs are recited to them﴾. The *ma* in ﴿that which does not harm them﴾ is either a relative pronoun or a qualifier. The *wa* in ﴿And they say, "These are our intercessors with Allah"﴾ is for conjunction with *wa-ya'budūna* (and they worship). They claimed that these would intercede for them with Allah, so He would not punish them for their sins. This is the utmost ignorance on their part, since they await intercession in the future from one who has neither benefit nor harm in the present. It has been said: by this intercession they meant the improvement of their worldly affairs. Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to respond on their behalf, so He said: ﴿Say, "Do you inform Allah of what He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?"﴾

Abu al-Sammal al-'Adawi read *tunabbi'ūna* (تُنْبِئُونَ) with light emphasis, from *anba'a yunbi'u*.

The rest read it with the doubled letter, from *nabba'a yunabbi'u*.

The meaning: Do you inform Allah that He has partners in His dominion who are worshipped as He is worshipped? Or do you inform Him that you have intercessors without His permission? Yet Allah, glorified is He, does not know for Himself any partner, or any intercessor without His permission, among all His creatures who are in His heavens and His earth. The upshot of this statement is that there is no such thing at all. In this there is a great deal of mockery of the disbelievers, which is not hidden. Then Allah, glorified is He, declared Himself free of their associating others with Him. This may be the beginning of a statement not included in the speech which Allah commanded His Messenger to answer them with, or it may be part of what the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to say to them in reply.

Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read ﴿'ammā yushrikūn﴾ (عَمّا يُشْرِكُونَ) with the third-person (yā') form. The rest read it with the second-person (tā') form. Abu 'Ubayd preferred the first reading.

His saying: ﴿And mankind was not but one community, then they differed﴾. Its tafsir has already been given in al-Baqarah.

The meaning: mankind was all but one community, affirming the oneness of Allah, glorified is He, and believing in Him. Then some became disbelievers and others remained believers, so some of them opposed others.

Al-Zajjaj said: They were the Arabs who were upon polytheism. He also said: every child is born upon *al-fitrah* (the natural disposition), and then they differed upon reaching maturity. But the first view is more apparent.

The intended meaning is not that every group innovated a religion of disbelief in opposition to the other. Rather, the intended meaning is that some disbelieved, and others remained upon *tawhid* (affirmation of Allah's oneness), as we have mentioned. ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾, which is that He, glorified is He, will not judge between them concerning what they differed about except on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿the matter would have been decided between them﴾ in this world, concerning what ﴿they were differing about﴾. But this has been prevented by the word which does not fail. It has also been said: the meaning of ﴿the matter would have been decided between them﴾ is by establishing the Hour upon them. It has been said: it would have been finished with their destruction. It has been said: the word is that Allah granted respite to this community, so He will not destroy them with punishment in this world. It has been said: the word is that He does not seize anyone except with a proof, which is the sending of messengers, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We would never punish until We have sent a messenger﴾ [al-Isra': 15]. It has been said: the word is His saying: "My mercy precedes My wrath."

'Isa ibn 'Umar read *la-qudiya* (لَقُضِيَ) in the active form (with Allah as subject understood as the one who decrees).

The rest read it in the passive form.

(p-617) Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ikrimah, who said: al-Nadr said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, al-Lat and al-'Uzza will intercede for me." So Allah revealed: ﴿Who does greater wrong than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies His signs? Indeed, the criminals will not succeed.﴾ ﴿And they worship besides Allah that which neither harms them nor benefits them﴾, to the end of the verse.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And mankind was not but one community, then they differed﴾, that Ibn Mas'ud said: "They were upon guidance." It was also reported that he recited it in this manner.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿And mankind was not but one community﴾, that he said: "Adam alone." ﴿Then they differed﴾, he said: "When one of the two sons of Adam killed his brother."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Suddi, concerning the verse, that he said: "The people were one religion upon the religion of Adam, then they disbelieved. Had your Lord not postponed them until the Day of Resurrection, the matter would have been decided between them."

The Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on Surah 10, verses 17–19:

His saying: ﴿Who does greater wrong than one who invents a lie against Allah?﴾ This is an interrogative with the sense of negation, meaning: no one does greater wrong than one who ﴿invents a lie against Allah﴾. The addition of *kadhiban* (a lie) although *iftira'* (invention) is never anything but a lie serves to show that this, besides being an invention against Allah, is a lie in itself. For an invention may be a lie only in its attribution, as when the sin of Zayd is attributed to 'Amr. Abu al-Su'ud mentioned the meaning of this in his tafsir. It has been said: this is part of his (ﷺ) response to the polytheists when they asked him to bring a Qur'an other than this Qur'an, or to change it. So He made clear to them that if he did that, it would be an invention against Allah, and no wrong is comparable to it. It has also been said: those who invent a lie against Allah are the polytheists, and those who deny the signs of Allah are the People of the Book. ﴿Indeed, the criminals will not succeed.﴾ This is a justification for the statement that there is no one more wrong than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies His signs. That is: they will not attain their objective, nor will they gain any good. The pronoun in *innahu* (indeed it) refers to the matter (*li-l-sha'n*), meaning: indeed the matter is this.

Then Allah, glorified is He, censured them for worshipping idols, and made clear that they neither benefit those who worship them nor harm those who do not worship them. So He said: ﴿And they worship besides Allah﴾, that is, transgressing beyond Allah, glorified is He, to worship others, not in the sense of abandoning His worship altogether. ﴿That which neither harms them nor benefits them﴾, that is, that which by its nature has neither harm nor benefit. It is the right of the one worshipped to reward those who obey him and punish those who disobey him. The *wa* (and) is for conjoining this sentence to the sentence ﴿And when Our signs are recited to them﴾. The *ma* in ﴿that which does not harm them﴾ is either a relative pronoun or a qualifier. The *wa* in ﴿And they say, "These are our intercessors with Allah"﴾ is for conjunction with *wa-ya'budūna* (and they worship). They claimed that these would intercede for them with Allah, so He would not punish them for their sins. This is the utmost ignorance on their part, since they await intercession in the future from one who has neither benefit nor harm in the present. It has been said: by this intercession they meant the improvement of their worldly affairs. Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to respond on their behalf, so He said: ﴿Say, "Do you inform Allah of what He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?"﴾

Abu al-Sammal al-'Adawi read *tunabbi'ūna* (تُنْبِئُونَ) with light emphasis, from *anba'a yunbi'u*.

The rest read it with the doubled letter, from *nabba'a yunabbi'u*.

The meaning: Do you inform Allah that He has partners in His dominion who are worshipped as He is worshipped? Or do you inform Him that you have intercessors without His permission? Yet Allah, glorified is He, does not know for Himself any partner, or any intercessor without His permission, among all His creatures who are in His heavens and His earth. The upshot of this statement is that there is no such thing at all. In this there is a great deal of mockery of the disbelievers, which is not hidden. Then Allah, glorified is He, declared Himself free of their associating others with Him. This may be the beginning of a statement not included in the speech which Allah commanded His Messenger to answer them with, or it may be part of what the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to say to them in reply.

Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read ﴿'ammā yushrikūn﴾ (عَمّا يُشْرِكُونَ) with the third-person (yā') form. The rest read it with the second-person (tā') form. Abu 'Ubayd preferred the first reading.

His saying: ﴿And mankind was not but one community, then they differed﴾. Its tafsir has already been given in al-Baqarah.

The meaning: mankind was all but one community, affirming the oneness of Allah, glorified is He, and believing in Him. Then some became disbelievers and others remained believers, so some of them opposed others.

Al-Zajjaj said: They were the Arabs who were upon polytheism. He also said: every child is born upon *al-fitrah* (the natural disposition), and then they differed upon reaching maturity. But the first view is more apparent.

The intended meaning is not that every group innovated a religion of disbelief in opposition to the other. Rather, the intended meaning is that some disbelieved, and others remained upon *tawhid* (affirmation of Allah's oneness), as we have mentioned. ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾, which is that He, glorified is He, will not judge between them concerning what they differed about except on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿the matter would have been decided between them﴾ in this world, concerning what ﴿they were differing about﴾. But this has been prevented by the word which does not fail. It has also been said: the meaning of ﴿the matter would have been decided between them﴾ is by establishing the Hour upon them. It has been said: it would have been finished with their destruction. It has been said: the word is that Allah granted respite to this community, so He will not destroy them with punishment in this world. It has been said: the word is that He does not seize anyone except with a proof, which is the sending of messengers, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We would never punish until We have sent a messenger﴾ [al-Isra': 15]. It has been said: the word is His saying: "My mercy precedes My wrath."

'Isa ibn 'Umar read *la-qudiya* (لَقُضِيَ) in the active form (with Allah as subject understood as the one who decrees).

The rest read it in the passive form.

(p-617) Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ikrimah, who said: al-Nadr said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, al-Lat and al-'Uzza will intercede for me." So Allah revealed: ﴿Who does greater wrong than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies His signs? Indeed, the criminals will not succeed.﴾ ﴿And they worship besides Allah that which neither harms them nor benefits them﴾, to the end of the verse.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And mankind was not but one community, then they differed﴾, that Ibn Mas'ud said: "They were upon guidance." It was also reported that he recited it in this manner.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿And mankind was not but one community﴾, that he said: "Adam alone." ﴿Then they differed﴾, he said: "When one of the two sons of Adam killed his brother."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Suddi, concerning the verse, that he said: "The people were one religion upon the religion of Adam, then they disbelieved. Had your Lord not postponed them until the Day of Resurrection, the matter would have been decided between them."

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on Surah 10, verses 20–23 (part 1 of 2)**

His saying: "And they say..." Here He, glorified is He, mentions a fourth kind of their shameful conduct. It is coordinated with His saying "and they worship..." (Yunus 18). He used the present tense (al-mudari') to bring the image of what they said before the mind.

It has been said: the speakers are the people of Makkah, as if they did not regard what had been revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of the striking signs and the overpowering miracles, of which the Qur'an alone would have sufficed as a clear proof and a decisive confirmation. That is: "Why was not a sign sent down to him from among the signs that we propose and demand of him, such as the raising of the dead, or turning the mountains into gold, and the like?" Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded him to answer them, so He said: ﴿Say: The unseen belongs only to Allah﴾, meaning: the sending down of a sign is part of the unseen, and Allah alone is the one specially knowing it, the one who alone holds it; neither I nor you nor any of His creatures has knowledge of it. ﴿So wait﴾ for the descent of what you have proposed of the signs; ﴿indeed I am with you among those who wait﴾ for its descent. It has also been said that the meaning is: wait for Allah's judgment between me and you, by manifesting the truth over falsehood.

His saying: ﴿And when We let people taste mercy after adversity has touched them, behold, they have a scheme against Our signs﴾. When He, glorified is He, made clear in the previous verse that they asked for a sign out of obstinacy, deceit and stubbornness, He confirmed this by what He mentions here: that when He lets them taste mercy from Himself after adversity has touched them, they respond to this great blessing with scheming against the signs of Allah. What is meant by letting them taste His mercy is that He widened their provisions and poured blessings upon them with rain and the good condition of fruits, after adversity had touched them through drought and straitened livelihoods. Yet they did not thank His blessing nor value it as it deserves; rather, they attributed it to their idols, which neither benefit nor harm, and they slandered the signs of Allah and devised every stratagem to repel them, and this is the meaning of the scheme (makr) in them.

The first idha (when) is conditional, and its answer is (﴿idha lahum makr﴾, "then they have a scheme"). It is a sudden idha (idha al-fuja'iyyah, the idha expressing something unexpected). Al-Khalil (al-Khalil ibn Ahmad) and Sibawayh mentioned this meaning.

Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded His Messenger to answer them, so He said: ﴿Say: Allah is swifter in scheming﴾, that is, swifter in punishment. The elative form (af'al al-tafdil, "swifter") indicates that their scheming was swift, but the scheming of Allah is swifter than theirs.

The sudden idha conveys the notion of speed, because the meaning is that they came upon the scheme unexpectedly, i.e., they carried it out suddenly and swiftly. Calling the punishment of Allah, glorified is He, a "scheme" is by way of mushakalah (rhetorical correspondence, using a word because of its association with another word), as has been established in several passages of the Noble Book, such as: ﴿Indeed Our messengers record what you scheme﴾.

Ya'qub in one transmission, and Abu 'Amr in one transmission, read yamkurun (with the yā', "they scheme," in the third person), while the rest read tamkurun (with the tā', "you scheme," in the second person).

The meaning is: the messengers of Allah, who are the angels, record the scheming of the disbelievers; this is not hidden from the angels who are the guardians. How then could it be hidden from the All-Knowing, the All-Aware? In this there is a severe warning to them. This sentence gives the reason for the sentence preceding it: since their scheming is manifest and not hidden, the punishment of Allah is inevitable. The meaning of this verse is close to the meaning of the preceding verse, ﴿And when harm touches man﴾, but this one has an addition: they do not restrict themselves to mere turning away, but seek to undermine the signs of Allah through the scheming they devise.

His saying: ﴿It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea﴾. He, glorified is He, set forth for these people an example so that the intended meaning might be fully uncovered. The meaning of His enabling them to travel on land is that they walk on their feet, which He created for them so that they might benefit from them, and that they ride the animals Allah created for their riding. The meaning of His enabling them to travel on the sea is that He inspired them to build the ships in which they ride in the depths of the sea, facilitated it for them, and warded off from them the causes of destruction.

Ibn 'Amir read ﴿He it is who makes you spread out (yanshurukum) in the sea﴾, with the nūn and an unpointed shīn, from nashr (spreading), as in His saying: ﴿then disperse in the land﴾ (al-Jumu'ah 10), meaning He spreads them in the sea, so He saves whom He wills and drowns whom He wills.

﴿Until, when you are in the ships and they sail with them﴾. The word al-fulk (ship) applies to the singular and the plural, and it may be masculine or feminine, and its verification has already been discussed. The verb jarayna means the ships, and "with them" means with the riders upon them. The word ḥattā (until) indicates the endpoint, and the endpoint is the content of the entire conditional sentence. The conditions considered in the protasis are three: the first is being in the ship; the second is its sailing with them by a good wind that is not violent; and the third is their rejoicing.

The conditions considered in the apodosis are three: the first is ﴿jā'athā﴾, i.e., "there came upon it [the ship]" a violent wind, or "there met it" a violent wind, that is, a violent wind encountered it. Al-'usf is the intensity of the blowing of the wind. The second is ﴿and the waves came upon them from every place﴾, that is, from all sides upon the ship, and what is meant is that they came upon those riding in it. The mawj (wave) is what rises of water above the sea. The third is ﴿they thought they were encompassed﴾, that is, the thought of destruction overcame them. Its root is the encirclement of an enemy around a people or a city, and this encirclement was made a figure for destruction even when it is not by an enemy, as here. The answer of idha in His saying ﴿when you are in the ships﴾ is the phrase (p. 618) "jā'athā" to the end of its clause. The saying ﴿they call upon Allah﴾ serves as a substitute for (ẓannū, "they thought") because this supplication from them occurred only at the thought of destruction, which was what prompted it; so it is a substitute with the substitution of inclusion (badal al-ishtimal), since it includes it. It is also possible that the clause ﴿they call﴾ is a new resumptive sentence, as if it were said: "What did they do?" and it was answered: "They called upon Allah." In His saying ﴿and they sail with them﴾ there is an iltifat (shift) from address to the third person; az-Zamakhshari, the author of al-Kashshaf, held that its benefit is intensification (mubalaghah).

Al-Razi said: the shift from the mode of address to the mode of the third person in this context is a sign of disdain and distancing, just as the reverse in His saying ﴿You alone we worship﴾ (al-Fatihah 5) is a sign of approval and closeness. The word mukhlisin (sincere) is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl): that is, they did not mix their supplication with any of the impurities, as had been their habit in other situations, when they would associate their idols with Allah in supplication. This sincerity was not due to belief in Allah alone, but in order that He might rescue them from the destruction they were on the verge of, since they knew that none but Allah, glorified is He, could save them.

In this there is evidence that creatures are naturally disposed to return to Allah in times of hardship, and that the one in distress has his supplication answered even if he is a disbeliever.

In this verse there is a clarification that these polytheists did not turn to their idols in such a state or in similar states. How strange, then, is what has occurred in Islam among groups who believe in the dead: when such a condition afflicts them at sea, they call upon the dead and do not make their supplication sincerely for Allah, as the polytheists did. This has reached us by mass transmission (tawatur) that yields certainty. So consider, may Allah guide you, what these satanic beliefs have done, to what place their adherents have arrived, to where Satan has driven them, and how he led them and gained power over them, until they submitted to him in a submission he would never have hoped for, not even in part, from the worshippers of idols. Surely we belong to Allah and to Him we return.

The lam in ﴿If You rescue us from this﴾ is the lam of oath preparation (al-lam al-muwatti'ah lil-qasam), meaning: saying this. The reference in His saying "from this" is to what they had fallen into of the verge of destruction at sea. The lam in ﴿we will surely be﴾ is the answer of the oath: that is, "we will surely be in every state among those who thank Your blessings that You have bestowed upon us," among them this blessing which we now seek from You to relieve us of and deliver us from. It has been said that this clause is the object of (da'aw, "they called").

When Allah rescued them from this trial into which they had fallen, and answered their supplication, they did not fulfill what they had promised of themselves. Rather, they acted as those who deny, not as those who give thanks, and they made transgression upon the earth without right take the place of gratitude.

The idha in ﴿behold, they transgress﴾ is the sudden idha: that is, they suddenly committed transgression upon the earth without right. Al-baghy means corruption, from the saying of the people "baghā al-jurḥ" (the wound spread) when it extended in corruption. The addition of "upon the earth" indicates that this corruption of theirs encompasses all regions of the earth. Although baghy would be contrary to being in right, since it cannot be except in falsehood, the addition of "without right" is an indication that they did this without any doubt in their own minds, but out of rebellion and obstinacy, because people may do such things on account of a doubt they hold to be true even when it is false.

His saying: ﴿O mankind, your transgression is only against yourselves — the enjoyment of the life of this world﴾. When He, glorified is He, mentioned that these people mentioned above transgress upon the earth without right, He mentioned the outcome of transgression and its evil consequence.

Ibn Ishaq, Hafs and al-Mufaddal read matā' (enjoyment) in the accusative, and the rest read it in the nominative.

Whoever reads it in the accusative makes what precedes it a complete sentence: that is, "your transgression is a calamity upon yourselves." So "your transgression" is the subject and "against yourselves" is its predicate, and "enjoyment" stands in the position of an emphatic infinitive (maṣdar), as if it were said: "you enjoy the enjoyment of the life of this world," and the infinitive together with the implied verb forms a new sentence (isti'naf). It has been said that matā' in the reading with the accusative is an adverb of time, like "the arrival of the pilgrim," meaning: at the time of the enjoyment of the life of this world. It has also been said that it is an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu), meaning: for the sake of the enjoyment of the life of this world. It has been said that it is in the accusative by removal of the preposition, meaning: like the enjoyment. It has also been said that it is in the accusative as a circumstantial state, as a verbal noun with the meaning of the passive participle, meaning: those who are given enjoyment. Most of these opinions regarding the justification of the accusative have been disputed.

As for whoever reads matā' in the nominative, making it the predicate of the subject, that is: "your transgression is the enjoyment of the life of this world." Then "against yourselves" is connected with the verbal noun. The estimated meaning is: "Your transgression against your likes, and those whose kind is your kind, is the enjoyment of the life of this world and its benefit, which has no lasting permanence." So what is meant by "yourselves" in this way is the sons of their kind, and it is expressed by "selves" because of the compassion that the kind feels toward its own kind. It has been said that the nominative of matā' is because it is a second predicate; it has been said that it is the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: "it is an enjoyment."

An-Nahhas said: On the reading with the nominative, bagh'ukum (your transgression) is nominative as the subject, and its predicate is "the enjoyment of the life of this world," and "against yourselves" is the object of the transgression. It is permissible that its predicate be "against yourselves," and a subject is implied: that is, "that is the enjoyment of the life of this world," or "it is the enjoyment of the life of this world." End of quotation.

Some of these aspects mentioned in justifying the nominative have also been disputed, in a discussion that is long and of no great benefit.

The conclusion is that when "against yourselves" is made the predicate of the subject, the meaning is that what occurs of transgression against others is also transgression against the transgressor himself, in terms of what the matter leads to, namely retaliation upon him in recompense for his transgression. If "enjoyment" is made the predicate, then what is meant is that the transgression of this human kind against one another is swift to vanish and near to dissolve, like all the goods of the life of this world, which go away quickly and perish swiftly, and have no great benefit or abundant profit.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned what the recompense for that transgression will be on the Day of Resurrection, with a severe warning, and said: ﴿Then to Us is your return﴾. The fronting of the predicate indicates restriction (al-qaṣr), and the meaning is: after this worldly life and its enjoyment, you will be returned to Allah, and He will recompense the evildoer for his evil and the doer of good for his good. ﴿Then We will inform you of what you used to do﴾ in the world, that is, We will inform you of what you used to do in the world of good and evil. What is meant by this is the recompense, as you say to one who has done evil: "I will inform you of what you did." In this there is the most severe warning and the most dreadful threat.

Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from al-Rabi', regarding His saying ﴿So wait, indeed I am with you among those who wait﴾, that he said: "He warned them of His punishment and His retribution."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh transmitted from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿And when We let people taste mercy after adversity has touched them, behold, they have a scheme against Our signs﴾, that he said: "It is mockery and denial."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 10, verses 20–23 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn Jurayj, concerning His words ﴿And they thought that they were encompassed by it﴾, that he said: "They perished."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Mardawayh related from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, with the following essential content: When the Prophet (ﷺ) declared the blood of a group of people lawful to shed on the Day of the Conquest (of Makkah), among them Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, Ikrimah fled from Makkah and boarded a ship, and a violent storm struck them. The people of the ship said to one another: "Devote yourselves sincerely (to God), for your gods will not avail you anything at all." Ikrimah said: "If sincere devotion will not save me at sea, nothing else will save me on land. O God, I make a covenant with You: if You grant me well-being from what I am in, I will go to Muhammad and place my hand in his hand, and I will surely find him forgiving and generous." So he came and embraced Islam.

Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym, al-Khatib in his History, and al-Daylami in Musnad al-Firdaws related from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Three things return upon their people: deceit (al-makr), breaking of oaths (al-nakth), and oppression (al-baghy)." Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited: ﴿O mankind, your oppression is only against yourselves﴾, ﴿and the evil of deceit does not encompass anyone except its own people﴾ [Fatir: 43], ﴿So whoever breaks his oath, he breaks it only to the detriment of himself﴾ [al-Hajj: 10].

Al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman related from Abu Bakrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Do not oppress, and do not be an oppressor, for God says: ﴿Your oppression is only against yourselves﴾."

Abu al-Shaykh related from Makhul, who said: "Three things, whoever has them, they are upon him: deceit, oppression, and breaking of oaths. God, glorified is He, said: ﴿Your oppression is only against yourselves﴾."

I say: These three that the Qur'an indicates return upon their doer should be joined by deception (al-khad'), for God says: ﴿They seek to deceive God and those who believe, but they deceive none except themselves﴾ [al-Baqarah: 9].

Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "If a mountain were to oppress another mountain, the oppressor among them would be crushed."

Ibn Mardawayh related from the hadith of Ibn Umar the like of it.

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on Surah 10, verses 20–23 (part 1 of 2)**

His saying: "And they say..." Here He, glorified is He, mentions a fourth kind of their shameful conduct. It is coordinated with His saying "and they worship..." (Yunus 18). He used the present tense (al-mudari') to bring the image of what they said before the mind.

It has been said: the speakers are the people of Makkah, as if they did not regard what had been revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of the striking signs and the overpowering miracles, of which the Qur'an alone would have sufficed as a clear proof and a decisive confirmation. That is: "Why was not a sign sent down to him from among the signs that we propose and demand of him, such as the raising of the dead, or turning the mountains into gold, and the like?" Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded him to answer them, so He said: ﴿Say: The unseen belongs only to Allah﴾, meaning: the sending down of a sign is part of the unseen, and Allah alone is the one specially knowing it, the one who alone holds it; neither I nor you nor any of His creatures has knowledge of it. ﴿So wait﴾ for the descent of what you have proposed of the signs; ﴿indeed I am with you among those who wait﴾ for its descent. It has also been said that the meaning is: wait for Allah's judgment between me and you, by manifesting the truth over falsehood.

His saying: ﴿And when We let people taste mercy after adversity has touched them, behold, they have a scheme against Our signs﴾. When He, glorified is He, made clear in the previous verse that they asked for a sign out of obstinacy, deceit and stubbornness, He confirmed this by what He mentions here: that when He lets them taste mercy from Himself after adversity has touched them, they respond to this great blessing with scheming against the signs of Allah. What is meant by letting them taste His mercy is that He widened their provisions and poured blessings upon them with rain and the good condition of fruits, after adversity had touched them through drought and straitened livelihoods. Yet they did not thank His blessing nor value it as it deserves; rather, they attributed it to their idols, which neither benefit nor harm, and they slandered the signs of Allah and devised every stratagem to repel them, and this is the meaning of the scheme (makr) in them.

The first idha (when) is conditional, and its answer is (﴿idha lahum makr﴾, "then they have a scheme"). It is a sudden idha (idha al-fuja'iyyah, the idha expressing something unexpected). Al-Khalil (al-Khalil ibn Ahmad) and Sibawayh mentioned this meaning.

Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded His Messenger to answer them, so He said: ﴿Say: Allah is swifter in scheming﴾, that is, swifter in punishment. The elative form (af'al al-tafdil, "swifter") indicates that their scheming was swift, but the scheming of Allah is swifter than theirs.

The sudden idha conveys the notion of speed, because the meaning is that they came upon the scheme unexpectedly, i.e., they carried it out suddenly and swiftly. Calling the punishment of Allah, glorified is He, a "scheme" is by way of mushakalah (rhetorical correspondence, using a word because of its association with another word), as has been established in several passages of the Noble Book, such as: ﴿Indeed Our messengers record what you scheme﴾.

Ya'qub in one transmission, and Abu 'Amr in one transmission, read yamkurun (with the yā', "they scheme," in the third person), while the rest read tamkurun (with the tā', "you scheme," in the second person).

The meaning is: the messengers of Allah, who are the angels, record the scheming of the disbelievers; this is not hidden from the angels who are the guardians. How then could it be hidden from the All-Knowing, the All-Aware? In this there is a severe warning to them. This sentence gives the reason for the sentence preceding it: since their scheming is manifest and not hidden, the punishment of Allah is inevitable. The meaning of this verse is close to the meaning of the preceding verse, ﴿And when harm touches man﴾, but this one has an addition: they do not restrict themselves to mere turning away, but seek to undermine the signs of Allah through the scheming they devise.

His saying: ﴿It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea﴾. He, glorified is He, set forth for these people an example so that the intended meaning might be fully uncovered. The meaning of His enabling them to travel on land is that they walk on their feet, which He created for them so that they might benefit from them, and that they ride the animals Allah created for their riding. The meaning of His enabling them to travel on the sea is that He inspired them to build the ships in which they ride in the depths of the sea, facilitated it for them, and warded off from them the causes of destruction.

Ibn 'Amir read ﴿He it is who makes you spread out (yanshurukum) in the sea﴾, with the nūn and an unpointed shīn, from nashr (spreading), as in His saying: ﴿then disperse in the land﴾ (al-Jumu'ah 10), meaning He spreads them in the sea, so He saves whom He wills and drowns whom He wills.

﴿Until, when you are in the ships and they sail with them﴾. The word al-fulk (ship) applies to the singular and the plural, and it may be masculine or feminine, and its verification has already been discussed. The verb jarayna means the ships, and "with them" means with the riders upon them. The word ḥattā (until) indicates the endpoint, and the endpoint is the content of the entire conditional sentence. The conditions considered in the protasis are three: the first is being in the ship; the second is its sailing with them by a good wind that is not violent; and the third is their rejoicing.

The conditions considered in the apodosis are three: the first is ﴿jā'athā﴾, i.e., "there came upon it [the ship]" a violent wind, or "there met it" a violent wind, that is, a violent wind encountered it. Al-'usf is the intensity of the blowing of the wind. The second is ﴿and the waves came upon them from every place﴾, that is, from all sides upon the ship, and what is meant is that they came upon those riding in it. The mawj (wave) is what rises of water above the sea. The third is ﴿they thought they were encompassed﴾, that is, the thought of destruction overcame them. Its root is the encirclement of an enemy around a people or a city, and this encirclement was made a figure for destruction even when it is not by an enemy, as here. The answer of idha in His saying ﴿when you are in the ships﴾ is the phrase (p. 618) "jā'athā" to the end of its clause. The saying ﴿they call upon Allah﴾ serves as a substitute for (ẓannū, "they thought") because this supplication from them occurred only at the thought of destruction, which was what prompted it; so it is a substitute with the substitution of inclusion (badal al-ishtimal), since it includes it. It is also possible that the clause ﴿they call﴾ is a new resumptive sentence, as if it were said: "What did they do?" and it was answered: "They called upon Allah." In His saying ﴿and they sail with them﴾ there is an iltifat (shift) from address to the third person; az-Zamakhshari, the author of al-Kashshaf, held that its benefit is intensification (mubalaghah).

Al-Razi said: the shift from the mode of address to the mode of the third person in this context is a sign of disdain and distancing, just as the reverse in His saying ﴿You alone we worship﴾ (al-Fatihah 5) is a sign of approval and closeness. The word mukhlisin (sincere) is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl): that is, they did not mix their supplication with any of the impurities, as had been their habit in other situations, when they would associate their idols with Allah in supplication. This sincerity was not due to belief in Allah alone, but in order that He might rescue them from the destruction they were on the verge of, since they knew that none but Allah, glorified is He, could save them.

In this there is evidence that creatures are naturally disposed to return to Allah in times of hardship, and that the one in distress has his supplication answered even if he is a disbeliever.

In this verse there is a clarification that these polytheists did not turn to their idols in such a state or in similar states. How strange, then, is what has occurred in Islam among groups who believe in the dead: when such a condition afflicts them at sea, they call upon the dead and do not make their supplication sincerely for Allah, as the polytheists did. This has reached us by mass transmission (tawatur) that yields certainty. So consider, may Allah guide you, what these satanic beliefs have done, to what place their adherents have arrived, to where Satan has driven them, and how he led them and gained power over them, until they submitted to him in a submission he would never have hoped for, not even in part, from the worshippers of idols. Surely we belong to Allah and to Him we return.

The lam in ﴿If You rescue us from this﴾ is the lam of oath preparation (al-lam al-muwatti'ah lil-qasam), meaning: saying this. The reference in His saying "from this" is to what they had fallen into of the verge of destruction at sea. The lam in ﴿we will surely be﴾ is the answer of the oath: that is, "we will surely be in every state among those who thank Your blessings that You have bestowed upon us," among them this blessing which we now seek from You to relieve us of and deliver us from. It has been said that this clause is the object of (da'aw, "they called").
